subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Boston Tea Party
description: A fast breakdown of The Boston Tea Party for builders.

hook.text: On December 16, 1773, American colonists dumped 342 chests of British tea into Boston Harbor—igniting a revolution.

buildup.text: Britain taxed tea without colonial representation. The tax wasn't huge, but the principle of control enraged colonists.

discovery.text: Disguised as Mohawk Indians, about 100 men boarded three ships and destroyed 46 tons of tea worth £10,000 (millions today).

twist.text: After the protest, drinking tea became unpatriotic. Americans switched to coffee—a shift that persists 250 years later.

climax.text: The Boston Tea Party was the spark for the American Revolution. A beverage tax helped create a nation.

punchline.text: 342 chests of tea, one harbor, a new nation. Coffee became America's patriotic drink.

quiz.question: How did the Boston Tea Party affect American beverage culture?
options: Drinking tea became unpatriotic — Americans switched to coffee
